```{r setup, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Load initial libraries and data
library(survival)
library(knitr)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(survminer)
data("heart", package = "survival")
```

```{r}
# Add simple time column calculated as difference between stop and start
heart <- heart %>%
  mutate(
    time = stop-start)

# Overview
summary(heart)

# Creation of dataset restricted to only patients who received heart transplants
heart <- heart[heart$transplant == 1, ]
summary(heart)
```

*3.2 Exploratory Data Analysis*

*Next, we analyze potential relationships between covariates of interest and days from enrollment until death (futime), in order to identify patterns or trends that may influence survival outcomes. The covariates examined include sex and FLC group, as these variables are clinically relevant and hypothesized to impact survival. Boxplots are used to visualize the distribution of survival times across levels of these categorical variables, providing initial insights into group differences.*

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(patchwork)

# First plot: Survival Time by Surgery
p1 <- ggplot(heart, aes(x = factor(surgery), y = time, fill = factor(surgery))) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.color = "red", outlier.shape = 16, outlier.size = 2) +
  labs(title = "Survival Time by Surgery", x = "Surgery", y = "Survival Time (days)") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("red", "green")) +
  theme_minimal()

# Second plot: Survival Time by Age Group
heart <- heart %>%
  mutate(
    trueage = age + 48,
    trueagegroup = factor(paste0(floor(trueage / 10) * 10, "-", floor(trueage / 10) * 10 + 9))
  )

p2 <- ggplot(heart, aes(x = factor(trueagegroup), y = time, fill = factor(trueagegroup))) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.color = "red", outlier.shape = 16, outlier.size = 2) +
  labs(title = "Survival Time by Age Group", x = "Age Group", y = "Survival Time (days)") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set3") +
  theme_minimal()

# Third plot: Survival Time by Year Group
heart <- heart %>%
  mutate(
    trueyear = year + 1967 + 305/365, #1 Nov 1967 was the 305th day of the year
    trueyeargroup = factor(floor(trueyear))
  )

p3 <- ggplot(heart, aes(x = factor(trueyeargroup), y = time, fill = factor(trueyeargroup))) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.color = "red", outlier.shape = 16, outlier.size = 2) +
  labs(title = "Survival Time by Year of Acceptance", x = "Year", y = "Survival Time (days)") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set3") +
  theme_minimal()

# Display one-by-one
p1
p2
p3
```


*The first boxplot shows relationship between survival time and sex reveals that females exhibit slightly higher median survival times compared to males, though the difference is small. Both groups, display similar overall survival distributions, suggesting that sex may not play a major role in survival outcomes for this cohort.*

*The second boxplot stratifies survival time by the free light chain (FLC) group. Groups 1–6 generally have longer survival times, with many extreme outliers present (e.g., individuals with survival times under 2,000 days). In contrast, groups 7–10 exhibit smaller median survival times and less variability. This pattern suggests a potential relationship between lower FLC group numbers and improved survival outcomes.*

*3.3 Survival Analysis*

*The Kaplan-Meier survival curves presented below explore the survival probabilities for different groups over time (in days). Panel A depicts the survival curve without stratifying by any covariates, providing an overall view of survival probabilities in the cohort. The survival probability decreases steadily over time, with the steepest decline occurring in the earlier periods, indicating a higher risk of death during the initial stages.*

*Panel B stratifies survival curves by the FLC group, revealing clear differences in survival outcomes between the groups. Higher groups exhibit steeper declines in survival probability, indicating poorer survival outcomes compared to lower groups, which maintain higher survival probabilities over the observed period. This trend suggests a possible protective effect associated with lower FLC group numbers, which warrants further investigation.*

*Panel C compares survival probabilities based on age group (Under 60 vs. 60+). The older age group (60+) demonstrates a sharper decline in survival probability compared to the younger group (Under 60), especially in the early stages of follow-up. This highlights age as a potential risk factor for poorer survival outcomes in this cohort.*

*Panel D illustrates survival curves by sex (Male vs. Female). Males experience a slightly steeper decline in survival probability compared to females, though the differences between the two groups are relatively minor. This suggests that while sex may influence survival outcomes, its impact appears to be less pronounced than that of FLC group or age.*

*Overall, these survival curves provide key insights into how survival outcomes differ across covariates, emphasizing the importance of FLC group and age in predicting survival probabilities. These findings set the stage for further statistical analyses, such as Cox proportional hazards modeling, to quantify the effects of these variables on survival outcomes.*

```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(survival)
library(survminer)
library(dplyr)
library(cowplot)

# Create age groups for analysis

# Kaplan-Meier estimator without covariates
km_fit_no_cov <- survfit(Surv(time, event) ~ 1, data = heart)

# Kaplan-Meier estimator stratified by Surgery
km_fit_surgery <- survfit(Surv(time, event) ~ surgery, data = heart)

# Kaplan-Meier estimator stratified by Age
km_fit_age_grp <- survfit(Surv(time, event) ~ trueagegroup, data = heart)

# Kaplan-Meier estimator stratified by Year
km_fit_year_grp <- survfit(Surv(time, event) ~ trueyeargroup, data = heart)

# Create Kaplan-Meier plots using ggsurvplot
plot_no_cov <- ggsurvplot(
  km_fit_no_cov,
  data = heart,
  conf.int = TRUE,
  title = "No Covariates",
  xlab = "Time (days)",
  ylab = "Survival Probability",
  ggtheme = theme_minimal(),
  legend = "none"
)

plot_surgery <- ggsurvplot(
  km_fit_surgery,
  data = heart,
  conf.int = TRUE,
  title = "Surgery",
  xlab = "Time (days)",
  ylab = "Survival Probability",
  ggtheme = theme_minimal(),
  legend.title = "Surgery"
)

plot_age_grp <- ggsurvplot(
  km_fit_age_grp,
  data = heart,
  conf.int = TRUE,
  title = "Age Group",
  xlab = "Time (days)",
  ylab = "Survival Probability",
  ggtheme = theme_minimal(),
  legend.title = "Age Group"
)

plot_year_grp <- ggsurvplot(
  km_fit_year_grp,
  data = heart,
  conf.int = TRUE,
  title = "Year",
  xlab = "Time (days)",
  ylab = "Survival Probability",
  ggtheme = theme_minimal(),
  legend.title = "Year"
)

# Extract the ggplot objects from the ggsurvplot outputs
p1 <- plot_no_cov$plot
p2 <- plot_surgery$plot
p3 <- plot_age_grp$plot
p4 <- plot_year_grp$plot

p1
p2
p3
p4
```

*Find median survival times*

```{r}
# Function to extract survival probabilities and confidence intervals at a specific time
compute_survival_at_time <- function(survfit_object, time_point) {
  # Extract survival summary for the specific time point
  survival_summary <- summary(survfit_object, times = time_point, extend = TRUE) #Modified code to compute survival summaries even if survival probability has already reached 0 at the time point
  
  # Create a data frame with results
  result <- data.frame(
    Group = rownames(summary(survfit_object)$table),
    Time = time_point,
    Survival_Prob = survival_summary$surv,
    Lower_CI = survival_summary$lower,
    Upper_CI = survival_summary$upper
  )
  
  return(result)
}

print(km_fit_no_cov)

print(km_fit_surgery)

print(km_fit_age_grp)
# Compute survival probabilities at 500 days for Age Group
survival_age_grp <- compute_survival_at_time(km_fit_age_grp, time_point = 500)
print("Survival Probabilities and 95% CI at 500 Days for Age Group:")
print(survival_age_grp)

print(km_fit_year_grp)
# Compute survival probabilities at 500 days for Year
survival_year_grp <- compute_survival_at_time(km_fit_year_grp, time_point = 500)
print("Survival Probabilities and 95% CI at 500 Days for Age Group:")
print(survival_year_grp)
```

```{r}
# Log-rank test for Surgery

print("Log-Rank Test for Surgery:")

# Log-rank test for Age Group
logrank_age_grp <- survdiff(Surv(time, event) ~ trueagegroup, data = heart)
print("Log-Rank Test for Age Group:")
print(logrank_age_grp)

# Log-rank test for Year
logrank_year_grp <- survdiff(Surv(time, event) ~ trueyeargroup, data = heart)
print("Log-Rank Test for Year:")
print(logrank_year_grp)
```

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(survival)

# Ensure relevant columns are factors
heart$surgery <- as.factor(heart$surgery)
heart$trueagegroup <- as.factor(heart$trueagegroup)

# Fit the Cox-PH model with surgery and age as covariates
cox_model <- coxph(Surv(time, event) ~ surgery + trueagegroup, data = heart)
summary(cox_model) # Display model summary

# --------------------
# Question 1: Estimate Hazard Ratio (HR) and 95% CI
# For surgery = 1, age = 30-39 vs. surgery = 0, age = 50-59
# --------------------

# Extract coefficients
coef_surgery <- coef(cox_model)["surgery1"] 
coef_trueagegroup3039 <- coef(cox_model)["trueagegroup30-39"]
coef_trueagegroup5059 <- coef(cox_model)["trueagegroup50-59"]

# Calculate log(HR)
log_hr <- (coef_surgery + coef_trueagegroup3039) - (coef_trueagegroup5059)
hr <- exp(log_hr) # Convert log hazard ratio to hazard ratio
cat("Hazard Ratio (surgery = 1, age = 30-39 vs. surgery = 0, age = 50-59):", hr, "\n")

# Variance for the combination of coefficients
var_surgery <- vcov(cox_model)["surgery1", "surgery1"]
var_trueagegroup <- vcov(cox_model)["trueagegroup30-39", "trueagegroup30-39"]
cov_surgery_age <- vcov(cox_model)["surgery1", "trueagegroup30-39"]

# Variance for log(HR)
var_log_hr <- var_surgery + var_trueagegroup + 2 * cov_surgery_age
se_log_hr <- sqrt(var_log_hr)

# Confidence interval (95%)
ci_lower <- exp(log_hr - 1.96 * se_log_hr)
ci_upper <- exp(log_hr + 1.96 * se_log_hr)
cat("95% CI for HR: [", ci_lower, ", ", ci_upper, "]\n")
```

```{r}
# --------------------
# Question 2: Likelihood Ratio Test for H0: beta surgery = 0
# --------------------

# Fit a reduced model without surgery
reduced_model <- coxph(Surv(time, event) ~ trueagegroup, data = heart)

# Perform a likelihood ratio test
lr_test <- anova(reduced_model, cox_model, test = "LRT")
cat("\nLikelihood Ratio Test for H0: βsurgery = 0:\n")
print(lr_test)
```


```{r}
# 1. Stratified Cox model by age group
stratified_model <- coxph(Surv(time, event) ~ surgery + strata(trueagegroup), data = heart)
summary(stratified_model)

# 2. Additive model including age group as a covariate
additive_model <- coxph(Surv(time, event) ~ surgery + trueagegroup, data = heart)
summary(additive_model)

# 3. Model with interaction term between surgery and age group
interaction_model <- coxph(Surv(time, event) ~ surgery * trueagegroup, data = heart)
summary(interaction_model)

# Compare models using AIC (or likelihood ratio tests)
cat("AIC for Stratified Model:", AIC(stratified_model), "\n")
cat("AIC for Additive Model:", AIC(additive_model), "\n")
cat("AIC for Interaction Model:", AIC(interaction_model), "\n")

# Optional: Perform likelihood ratio test for interaction term
anova(additive_model, interaction_model, test = "LRT")
```

```{r}
library(survival)
library(survminer)

# 1. Schoenfeld residuals to check proportional hazards assumption
# Test for non-proportionality of hazards
ph_test <- cox.zph(cox_model)
print(ph_test) # Display test results

par(mfrow = c(1,2))
# Plot scaled Schoenfeld residuals for each covariate
plot(ph_test, var = "trueagegroup", resid = TRUE, main = "Schoenfeld Residuals for Age")
plot(ph_test, var = "surgery", resid = TRUE, main = "Schoenfeld Residuals for Surgery")
```

```{r}
# 2. Martingale residuals to assess functional form of covariates
# Extract Martingale residuals
martingale_resid <- residuals(cox_model, type = "martingale")

par(mfrow = c(1,2))
# Plot Martingale residuals against age
plot(heart$trueage, martingale_resid, 
     xlab = "Age", ylab = "Martingale Residuals", 
     main = "Martingale Residuals vs Age")
abline(h = 0, col = "red")

plot(heart$surgery, martingale_resid, 
     xlab = "Surgery", ylab = "Martingale Residuals", 
     main = "Martingale Residuals vs Surgery")
abline(h = 0, col = "red")
```

```{r}
# 3. Deviance residuals to identify outliers
# Extract deviance residuals
deviance_resid <- residuals(cox_model, type = "deviance")

# Plot deviance residuals
plot(deviance_resid, 
     ylab = "Deviance Residuals", xlab = "Observation Index", 
     main = "Deviance Residuals")
abline(h = 0, col = "red")
abline(h = 2, col = "gray", lty = 2)
abline(h = -2, col = "gray", lty = 2)

# Highlight potential outliers (e.g., top 5 largest residuals)
potential_outliers <- which(abs(deviance_resid) > 2)
cat("Potential Outliers (Indices):\n", potential_outliers, "\n")
```

```{r}
# Subset outliers
outliers <- heart[potential_outliers, ]

# Compare covariates: Age, Survival, and FLC Group
par(mfrow = c(1, 3)) # Arrange plots side-by-side

# Age comparison
boxplot(heart$trueage, outliers$trueage,
        names = c("Full Dataset", "Outliers"),
        main = "Age Comparison",
        ylab = "Age")

# Age comparison
boxplot(heart$surgery, outliers$surgery,
        names = c("Full Dataset", "Outliers"),
        main = "Surgery Comparison",
        ylab = "Surgery")

# Boxplot: Survival times comparison
boxplot(heart$time, 
        outliers$time, 
        names = c("Full Dataset", "Outliers"),
        main = "Survival Times for Outliers",
        ylab = "Survival Time")
```
